title: Commercial Fusion Energy in 2026

stats.label: U.S. target for fusion deployment
stats.detail: DOE's Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap, released in June, is the central plank of the federal strategy.

stats.label: Record private fusion funding
stats.detail: Raised worldwide in the 12 months to July 2026, according to the Fusion Industry Association.

stats.label: ITER sector modules installed
stats.detail: Two-thirds of the tokamak core now in place, almost six months ahead of schedule.

stats.label: U.S. fusion companies
stats.detail: Many are developing tokamaks or stellarators; others pursue laser-based inertial confinement.

stats.label: FES appropriation for FY2027
stats.detail: Below the $805.7 million enacted, and far under the $1.1 billion authorized in 2022 legislation.

stats.label: Tritium half-life
stats.detail: Tritium is scarce on Earth; future reactors plan lithium breeding blankets to generate it.

quotes.text: "The plan isn't the problem. We all agree on the plan. The X factor is the funding. If we underfund the U.S. fusion program and we cut vital scope, we can all watch the timeline to commercialisation slip."
quotes.source: Robb Hughes, Realta Fusion, via Reuters

quotes.text: "Installing six sector modules is not simply a question of repeating the same operation six times."
quotes.source: Sergio Orlandi, Head of the ITER Construction Project

quotes.text: ITER is "primarily an exploratory science initiative and is not designed or intended to produce electricity."
quotes.source: CRS R48866, Toward Commercial Fusion Energy

quotes.text: Private developers have not yet achieved "net energy gain" — where a fusion reaction produces more energy than was used to start and sustain it.

takeaway: Fusion's assembly milestones are arriving ahead of schedule; its funding milestones are not.
